limitations: The study's purpose was not to provide an exhaustive account of the many techniques for integrating biophilic design features into buildings, indicating a scope limitation.
minimum_safe_summary: This paper, presented as an original research paper using a qualitative methodology combining case studies and extensive literature reviews, explores the economic benefits of biophilic design in the workplace. It argues that integrating nature-inspired architectural elements significantly enhances employee well-being and productivity, leading to substantial economic advantages such as reduced absenteeism, lower healthcare costs, heightened productivity, and improved employee retention. Key findings indicate that natural light, indoor plants, views of nature, and natural materials positively impact mental acuity, creativity, stress reduction, and sleep quality, while also improving air quality and overall job satisfaction. The paper highlights that biophilic design is a cost-effective investment for businesses. A stated limitation is that the study does not provide an exhaustive account of all biophilic design integration techniques.
